WRITTEN ANSWERS TO STARRED QUESTIONS 
Management of Kendriya Vidyalayas 
 *421. SHRI K.B. KRISHNA MURTHY:                          
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA: 
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan (KVS) has failed to cater to 
the educational needs of the children and whether there are large scale irregularities in the 
management of the schools; 
(b) whether it is also a fact that infrastructure facilities, such as buildings, 
*Not recorded. 
2 

[25 April, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
playgrounds, laboratories, computers, drinking water and sewerage etc. are 
lacking in many schools despite enhancement of monthly rates of contribution 
from the students; and 
(c) the details of the steps initiated by Government to strengthen control and 
monitoring of KVS over functioning of the schools? 
THE MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (SHRI 
ARJUN SINGH): (a) No, Sir. Through a network of 914 Kendriya Vidyalayas 
functioning across the country, the Ke ndriya Vidyalaya Sangathan (KVS) has 
been able to offer quality education to the children and wards of Central 
Government employees, as well as to others. Some of the KVS schools are in 
the military and project sect ors. With a view towards extending this facility to 
more areas, Government is committed to increasing the number of KVs. Some 
irregularities with regard to recruitment of teachers, diversion of funds, concessions 
to private parties, purchase of land, etc. have come to light and are under detailed 
enquiry. 
(b) No, Sir. While Kendriya Vidyalayas are initially opened in temporary/ hired 
buildings, once the Sangathan construct their permanent buildings, the necessary 
infrastructure facilities are provided. As on the 1st April 2005, only 207 out of 
a total of 932 Kendriya Vidyalayas were functioning in temporary/hired 
buildings. 
(c) KVS is administered and controlled, by a Board of Governors chaired by the 
Minister for Human Resource Development which takes all decisions towards 
ensuring proper functioning of the Sangathan and of the schools. With a view to 
improving the system, Government has recently issued the following 
instructions:— 
(i) Commissioner, KVS along with senior officers should be available on 
previous notified dates for those teaching and non-t eaching staff who 
approach them with personal problems for redressal of their legitimate 
grievances. 
(ii) All those candidates selected earlier and regarding which selection 
complaints have been received, w ill be provisionally appointed pending 
enquiry, with a view to ensuring that  a sufficient number of teachers are 
available. 
3 

RAJYA SABHA [25 April, 2005] 
(iii) KVS will provide adequate fire safety measures in all KVs. 
(iv) Meeting of the BOG and other Sub-committees will be held at regular intervals. 
National Mission for Urban Poor 
*422. SHRI V. HANUMANTHA RAO: Will the Minister of URBAN 
EMPLOYMENT AND POVERTY ALLEVIATION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government propose to form a National Mission for basic services to 
urban poor; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether existing institutions would be scrapped in favour of the National 
Mission; 
(d) to what extent Government propose to remove all urban slums in the next five 
years; and 
(e) the details of the schedule of targets for removal of urban slums? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF URBAN 
EMPLOYMENT AND POVERTY ALLEVIATION (KUMARI SELJA): (a) to (e) 
Government is considering to set up a National Urban Renewal Mission to improve the quality 
of urban life. It also proposes to take a comprehensive view to provide basic services to the 
urban poor towards fulfilment of their basic needs, including security of tenure, housing, water 
supply, sanitation, education, health care and social security cover. The detailed modalities 
for the proposed Mission are being worked out.

Judge-population ratio 
*427. DR. ALLADI P. RAJKUMAR: Will the Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE be 
pleased to state: 
(a) the number of judges of High Courts and Subordinate Courts per one lakh 
population; 
(b) whether Government propose to increase the number of judges per lakh of 
population; and 
(c) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF LAW AND JUSTICE (SHRI H.R. BHARDWAJ): (a) to (c) The 
present judge strength in India is approximately 13 per million population. 
8 

[25 April, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
2. The last Triennial Review of the Judge strength of various High Courts was 
held in 2003. As a result, it was decided to increase the Judge strength of various 
High Courts from the existing strength of 655 to 749 Judges. 
3. The Supreme Court, in its judgement of 21st March, 2002, in the case of 
All India Judges'Association & Ors Vs. Union of India & Ors, had directed that 
an increase in the Judge strength from existing 10.5 or 13 per 10 lakh people to 
50 judges per 10 lakh people should be effected and implemented within a period 
of five years in a phased manner to be determined and directed by the Union 
Ministry of Law. The Court had also directed that the existing vacancies in the 
Subordinate Courts at all levels should be filled. 
 
3.1 The Central Government have filed an affidavit in the Supreme Court 
praying that the increase in judge strength in the Union Territories for which 
Central Government is administratively responsible be allowed based on workload 
and pendency of cases. The matter is sub-judice. 
3.2 All State Governments are also party to this case. Under article 235 of the 
Constitution of India, the administrative control over the members of subordinate 
judiciary in the States vests with concerned High Court and the State 
Government. Accordingly, the Central Government has requested all the State 
Governments for taking necessary action to increase the judge strength as per 
the direction of the Supreme Court, and also to fill up the vacant posts of judicial 
officers on urgent basis.

Literacy ratio 
†*431. SHRI P.K. MAHESHWARI: Will the Minister of HUMAN 
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have conducted any study to ascertain the literacy ratio of 
male and female in the country; 
(b) if so, the details thereof for the last five years, State-wise; 
(c) whether the female literacy rate in Madhya Pradesh happens to be lower than that 
of the other States; and 
(d) whether any separate arrangement has been made to increase the female literacy 
in the State? 
THE MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (SHRI 
ARJUN SINGH): (a) and (b) The literacy rates are compiled and released decennially by 
the Registrar General & Census Commissioner of India. A statement indicating the State-
wise literacy rates of males and females, as per the Census 2001 data, is given in the 
enclosed Statement (See below). 
(c) and (d) The female literacy rate of Madhya Pradesh, as per Census 2001 data, is 
50.29% as against the national level of 53.67%. The female literacy rate of Madhya Pradesh 
increased from 29.35% in 1991 to 50.29% in 2001, an increase of 20.94 percentage 
points. 
The following steps have been taken to further improve the female literacy in the 
State:— 
(i)      A Mahila Padhna Badhna Andolan was implemented by the 
State Government during 2002-03 in which 17,02,908 women 
              were made literate.

Badhna Abhiyan is being implemented to cover 8 lakh illiterate women.

literacy districts of the State to cover an estimated 14 lakh illiterate 
women.

*434. SHRI JANESHWAR MISHRA: 
SHRIMATI SUKHBUNS KAUR: 
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the tendency of committing suicide due to failure 
in examinations or poor results and tension is on the rise among the students; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether Government have ever given serious consideration to the matter    
. 
(d) if so, the details thereof; 
(e) the year-wise details of the students committing suicide; and 
(f) the steps taken so far by Government to check it? 
THE MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (SHRI 
ARJUN SINGH): (a) and (b) The attention of the Government has been drawn 
from time to time to the problem of increasing stress levels among students 
during examinations and instances of some students committing suicides due 
to failure in examinations and stress. There are various other contributing 
factors to such levels including parental pressure, increasing competition and 
the fast changing social and economic conditions. 
(c) to (f) Yes, Sir. While no data regarding the number of suicides 
committed by the students is maintained centrally, the Ministry is deeply 
concerned with the issue of high stress level among students caused by the public 
examinations at the end of class X and XII conducted by various boards, Joint 
Entrance Examinations for IITs and other entrance examinations. To address 
the question of promoting equality in access to education as also allow the 
students to have a stress free environment of joyful learning, the Ministry had 
convened a meeting rece ntly with Eminent Educationists, Principals, 
representatives from premier institutions such as the Indian Institutes of 
Technology and Indian Institutes of Management, Heads of the Boards of 
Examination and 
18 

[25 April, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
others. It was unanimously agreed that  there must by systemic reforms to 
eliminate exam-related stress. It was also felt that a national consensus on the 
issue should be reached through wider discussion. 
In the context of review of the National Curriculum Framework, a 
National Steering Group has been constituted by NCERT under the 
chairmanship of Prof. Yashpal, which is being facilitated by 21 National Focus 
Groups. One of the Focus Group will address the issue of carrying out public 
examination reforms. 
The Standing Committee of the NT Council in a meeting held on the 5th 
March, 2005 discussed the issue of stress caused by the Joint Entrance 
Examination (JEE) and the mushrooming of coaching institutes. It was decided 
that IIT Directors will come out with concrete proposals for bringing out reforms 
in the JEE. 
In pursuance of the decision taken in the meeting, the Council of Boards of 
School Education in India (COBSE) is organizing a one day conference on the 1st 
May, 2005 of the chairmen of the School Education Boards to deliberate further 
and evolve a national consensus on this issue. Once the national consensus is 
reached, the process of examination reforms will be initiated before the 
conduct of the 2006 examinations.

Objectives of the ICDS 
*437. SHRIMATI AMBIKA SONI: 
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA: 
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that despite full utilisation of funds allocated under 
the Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS), a large number of children 
under the age of five die every month due to malnutrition while the main aim of 
ICDS is to lower the infant mortality; 
(b) if so, whether Government have looked into the working of ICDS and if so, 
the outcome thereof; and 
(c) whether Government have identified the factors responsible for failure 
of the ICDS and the details of the steps taken/proposed to be taken to improve 
ICDS and to bring down infant mortality rate? 
20 

[25 April, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
THE MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT (SHRI 
ARJUN SINGH): (a) to (c) The Integrated Child Development Services 
(ICDS) Scheme aims at holistic development of children below 6 years. Reduction 
in the incidence of mortality among children is one of the objectives of the 
Scheme. The Scheme which was launched in 1975 in 33 blocks, on an 
experimental basis, now covers 5652 blocks in the country. Infant Mortality Rate 
(IMR) has declined from 110 in 1981 per thousand live birth to 63 in 2002. 
Similarly, under-5 mortality has declined from 161 in 1983 to 87 in 2003. 
Moreover, as per evaluation of the ICDS Scheme by National Council for 
Applied Economic Research (NCAER) in 1998-99, there has been a significant 
impact of the Scheme in reduction of IMR. It would, therefore, not be correct to 
say that the Scheme has been a failure. 
It has, however, been a constant endeavour of the Government to make the 
Scheme more effective. The steps taken in  this direction, in the recent past, 
include, proposed expansion of the ICDS Scheme to bring uncovered 
habitations/settlements within its ambit, as per Government's commitment 
contained in the National Common Minimum Programme (NCMP); doubling 
of financial norms for supplementary nutrition; provision of Central assistance to 
States for Supplementary Nutrition; doubling of honoraria of Anganwadi 
Workers and Helpers; introduction of Anganwadi Karyakartri Bima Yojana'; a 
scheme of Awards for exemplary work done by Anganwadi workers; better 
coordination and monitoring at State, District, Block and Village level 
amongst ICDS, Health and Elementary Education functionaries, etc. 
Government is also implementing several other programmes/schemes viz. 
National Diarrhoea Disease Control Programme; National Acute Respiratory 
Infection (ARI) Control Programme; Vitamin-A Supplementation; Iron and 
FolicAcid Supplementation; Promotion of Breast feeding; Complementary 
feeding from six months of life; Integrated Management of Neonatal and 
Childhood Illness etc. to address the problem of infant and child mortality in the 
country.

Functioning of BRPSE 
3265. SHRI JIBON ROY: Will the Minister of HEAVY INDUSTRIES 
AND PUBLIC ENTERPRISES be pleased to state: 
(a) what are the functions of Board for Reconstruction of Public Sector 
Enterprises (BRPSE) and how it is different from BIFR; 
(b) the details of the cases referred to BRPSE so far; 
(c) whether Government have referred the cases of Hindustan Cables, B.O.G. 
Ltd., etc. to the Board for Reconstruction of Public Sector Enterprises; and 
(d) if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF HEAVY INDUS-
TRIES AND PUBLIC ENTERPRISES (SHRI SONTOSH MOHAN DEV): (a) 
The functions of the Board for Reconstruction of Public Sector Enterprises 
(BRPSE) are:- to advise the Government on ways and means for strengthening 
Public Sector Enterprises in general and making them more autonomous and 
professional; to consider restructuring of CPSEs and suggest ways and means 
for funding such restructuring schemes; to examine the revival/restructuring 
proposals of sick/loss making CPSEs for their turn around and to make suitable 
recommendations related thereto; to advise the Government on 
disinvestment/closure/sale of chronically loss making companies which cannot be 
revived and advise the Government about sources of fund for the payment of 
all legitimate dues and compensation to workers and other costs of closures; to 
monitor incipient sickness in CPSEs and advise the Govt, on such other matters 
as may be assigned to it. 
BRPSE may consider cases of non-industrial as well as incipient sick CPSEs 
and advise Government on ways and means of strengthening the public sector 
enterprises and making them more autonomous and professional. Board for 
Industrial and Financial Reconstruction (BIFR) is a statutory body set up under 
Sick Industrial Companies (Special Provisions) Act (SICA), 1985 to sanction 
suitable revival/rehabilitation packages in case of sick industrial companies - 
both CPSEs as well as Private Sector companies.

(c) NO, Sir 
(d) The administrative Ministry/Department is responsible for preparing a

after due consultations with all the stakeholders and refer the proposal to

49 

RAJYA SABHA [25 April, 2005]

The guidelines laid lown by the Supreme Court provide definition of

Statement 
Details of initiatives taken by the Government to implement the guidelines 
laid down by the Supreme Court and to create awareness about the issue of 
sexual harassment at workplace 
The Government has requested all the Central Ministries/Departments, Chief 
Secretaries of all the State Governme nts/Union Territory Administrations, 
Universities/Institutions, Central Board of Secondary Education, All India 
Council of Technical Education to constitute complaints committees and to ensure 
that the guidelines laid down by the Supreme Court in the Vishaka case for 
prevention of sexual harassment at workplace are implemented. 
The National Commission for Women (NCW) formulated a Code of 
Conduct for Workplace, putting down  the Supreme Court's guidelines 
mentioned above in a simple manner. This has been circulated to State 
Commissions for Women, Non-Governmental Organisations, the apex bodies 
for the Corporate Sector, Public Sector Undertakings, Media, 
Ministries/Departments and other institutions. 
The NCW has instituted a series of interactive meetings with Public Sector 
Undertakings/Banks/Universities/Educational/Institutions/Hotels/ Media etc. to 
assess the extent of implementation of the guidelines. 
50 

[25 April, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
Department of Public Enterprises issued circular in May, 1998 to all 
administrative Ministries/Departments concerned with Central Public Sector 
Establishments to direct the Chief Executives of CPSEs under their 
administrative control for adherence and compliance of the Supreme Court's 
guidelines on prevention of sexual harassment by making amendments in the 
CDA Rules of the CPSEs. 
A Central Committee headed by Secretary, Department of Women and Child 
Development has been constituted in the Department of Women and Child 
Development to review the implementation of the guidelines. During the year 
2004, the Committee met on 27-7-2004. In pursuance of the meeting, all 
Ministries/Departments and State Governments/UT Ad-ministrations were 
again requested to ensure setting up of complaints committee and to ensure its 
proper functioning. 
So far as implementation of the Supreme Court guidelines in regard to setting 
up of complaints committee in small establishments like shops and call centres 
are concerned, section 1(3) of the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 
1947 applies to every establishment wherein 100 and more workers are 
employed. However, appropriate Government may apply the provisions of the 
Act to any industrial establishment employing less than 100 persons. Since the 
State Governments are the appropriate Government in respect of commercial 
establishments like shops and calI centers, necessary instruction have been issued 
by the Ministry of Labour and Employment during January, 2005 to all Labour 
Secretaries asking them to suitable action to apply the provisions of the Industrial 
Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946 to small establishments like call centres 
and shops in the unorganised sector. 
The Central Civil Services (Conduct) Rules, 1964 have been amended to 
include sexual harassment as misconduct. The Central Civil Services (Control, 
Classification and Appeal) Rules, 1965 have been amended during July, 2004 to 
provide that the Complaints Committee established in each Ministry or 
Department of Office for inquiring into complaints of sexual harassment shall 
be deemed to be the inquiry authority appointed by the disciplinary authority and 
the Complaints Committee shall hold the inquiry as far as practicable in 
accordance with the procedure laid down in these rules (i.e. the procedure for 
holding inquiry into disciplinary proceedings for award of a major penalty). 
51 

RAJYA SABHA [25 April, 2005] 
The Department of Women and Child Development is examining a draft legislation 
to prohibit sexual harassment of women at workplace. 
Amendment have been made to the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 
1946 so that the sexual harassment of women at workplace in the private sector could 
constitute an offence for which a workman is liable for disciplinary action. 
Necessary instruction have been issued by the Ministry of labour and Employment 
during January, 2005 to all State Labour Secretaries asking them to take suitable action to 
apply the provisions of the Industrial Em-ployment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946 to 
small establishments like call centres and shops in the unorganised sector. 
Media campaign has been undertaken by the Department of Women and Child 
Development to create awareness on various issues concerning women and children, including 
compliance with the Supreme Courts guidelines on the prevention of sexual harassment of 
women at workplace.

Representation of women in Print and Electronic Media 
3270. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) the States that have set up Advisory Committee to assist the enforcement 
machinery under the Indecent Representation of Women Act, 1986; 
(b) whether it is a fact that indecent representation of women in print and electronic 
media violates one of the fundamental duties of the constitution and also leading to increase 
the violence against women; and 
(c) if so, the details thereof and the action taken and proposed to be taken in this 
regard? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRIMATI KANTI SINGH): (a) The Indecent Representation of 
Women (Prohibition) Act, 1986 or the rules framed thereunder do not have any provision for 
the constitution of any kind of advisory committee either at the central or state level for any 
purpose under the Act. 
(b) The indecent representation of women in any form in the print and electronic 
media violates Article 51A(e) of the Constitution which specifically enjoins that it is the 
fundamental duty of every citizen to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of 
women. However, there is no spe-cific details/data to support the view that indecent 
representation of women is leading to increase in violence against women. 
(c) The required information is given in the enclosed Statement. 
Statement 
Action taken by the Government to check depiction of obscenity in                                           
the electronic and print media 
As regards the electronic media, Pras ar Bharati has both Programme and 
Advertisement Codes which inter-alia, prohibit telecast/broadcast of any programme or 
advertisement, which contains anything obscene. Doordarshan and All India Radio 
abide by the codes while telecasting/ broadcasting their programmes. 
53 

RAJYA SABHA [25 April, 2005] 
The programmes of all Satellite Channels, when transmitted through cable television 
networks in the country, are required to adhere to the programmes and advertising codes 
presoribed under the Cable Television Networks (Regulation) Act, 1995 and Rules 
framed there under. The Programme Code prohibits carriage of such programmes in Cable 
Service, which offend good taste or decency, contain anything obscene and are not 
suitable for unrestricted public exhibition. Programmes meant for children are 
prohibited from carrying explicit scenes of violence. 
The Government has constituted a Committee to look into complaints regarding any 
programme of any channel not being in conformity with the prescribed Programme Code. 
Government has constituted another committee to look into violations of the 
Advertising Code. 
In so far as the Print media is concerned, the Press Council of India (PCI) is a 
statutory authority established for preserving the freedom of the Press and for maintaining and 
improving the standards of newspapers and news agencies in India. PCI has set the Norms 
for Journalistic Conduct according to which Newspapers/Journalists shall not publish anything 
which is obscene, vulgar or offensive to public and not in good taste.

Macaulay education system 
†3291. SHRI ISAM SINGH: Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 
77 

RAJYA SABHA [25 April, 2005] 
(a) whether the structure of Macaulay Education System was based on 
inequality; 
(b) if so, the structure of education system in the present situation; and 
(c) Government's action plan to bring uniformity in the Indian education 
system? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRI MD. ALI ASHRAF FATMI): (a) to (c) The structure 
of the education system in pre-independence India instituted on the 
linessuggested by Macaulay was geared basically to provide manpower support, 
particularly at the lower levels, for the British Raj to carry out its 
administrative functions. The National Policy on Education formulated in 
1968, marked a significant step in the history of education in the post-
Independence India. Subsequently, the National Policy on Education (NPE), 1986 
was adopted, which was further modified in 1992, keeping in view the 
developments and expansion of educati onal facilities, as also need and the 
aspirations of the country. The NPE and its Programme of Action, 1992 
provides a comprehensive framework that guides the development of education 
in its entirety in the country. 
The extent National Policy on Education (NPE) implies that, up to a given 
level, all students irrespective of caste, creed, location or sex have access to 
education of a comparable quality. It includes a common educational structure, 
a national curriculum framework and minimum levels of learning for each stage of 
education. The NPE also envisages separate and special provisions for the 
education of disadvantaged sections of the society, and several schemes were 
launched by way of central interventions for meeting the needs of the 
educationally backward classes. 
With the passing of the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002, free 
and compulsory education for all children in the 6—14 year age group is 
now a Fundamental Right under Article—21-Aof the Constitution. The 
enabling legislation to enforce the Right, when enacted, would provide the 
supporting statutory mechanism for universalisation of elementary education. 
The National Policy on Education, while encouraging non-governmental and 
voluntary efforts including social activist groups in the field of education, calls for 
steps to prevent commercialization of education. Several Central 
78 

[25 April, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
schemes encourage the participation of NGOs/VAs to supplement     
governmental efforts. 
The National Council of Educational Research & Training (NCERT) has 
recently initiated the review of Nati onal Curriculum Framework for School 
Education (NCFSE), which has become due for review. The University 
Grants Commission (UGC), All India Council for Technical Education 
(AICTE) and National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE), have been set up 
as statutory bodies to ensure proper maintenance of norms and standards in 
Higher Education, Technical and Management Education and Teacher 
Education, respectively. 
The Government has reconstituted the Central Advisory Board of 
Education (CABE) and, seven CABE Committees have been set up on the 
subjects of (i) Free and Compulsory Education Bill and other issues related to 
Elementary Education; (ii) Girls Education and the Common School System; 
(iii) Universalisation of Secondary Education; (iv) Autonomy of Higher Education 
Institutions; (v) Integration of Culture Education in the School Curriculum; (vi) 
Regulatory Mechanism for the Text Books and parallel text taught in schools 
outside the Government System; and (vii) Financing of Higher and Technical 
Education.

Policy for development of Higher Education 
†3313. SHRI RAMADHAR KASHYAP: Will the Minister of HUMAN 
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are contemplating to declare a separate policy for the 
development of higher education; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) if not, the reasons therefor; 
(d) whether it is a fact that development of higher education has come to a halt during 
the past several years in the absence of education policy; and 
(e) if so, Government's reaction thereto?                                                                
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 
103 
 

RAJYA SABHA [25 April, 2005] 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRI MD. ALIASHRAF FATMI): (a) to (e) The National 
Policy on Education, 1986 (as modified in 1992) guides the educational 
development in its entirety and covers all levels of education including higher 
education. As such, separate policy for the development of higher education is 
not considered necessary. There has been all round development at all levels of 
education including higher education. The higher education system has increased 
about fourteen-fold in terms of the number of universities and about thirty-three-fold 
in terms of the number of colleges, in comparison to the number at the time of 
independence. The University Grants Commission, a statutory organisation, looks 
after the coordination, determination and maintenance of standards of university 
education. 
Seven Committees of the Central Advisory Board of Education have since 
been set up on various issues relating to education sector. For higher 
education, a Committee has been constituted on the subject of "Autonomy of 
Higher Education Institutions" to suggest measures for enhancing the 
autonomy of higher education institutions, especially those with potential for 
excellence and to institutionalise regulatory provisions for promoting autonomy 
and accountability of higher education institutions. Another Committee on the 
subject of "Financing of Higher and Technical Education" has been set up to 
examine the adequacy of investments in Higher/Technical Education and to find 
ways of augmenting the resource flow in Higher Education, the question of a 
fair share of 6% of GDP for Education, and to suggest the ways of encouraging 
and regulating private participation and investments in Higher/Technical 
Education.

3318. SHRI S.P.M. SYED KHAN : Will the Minister of HUMAN 
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether there is an alarming rise in sexual abuse of children in the 
country, particularly in Goa; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) the number of cases of sexual abuse of children registered across the 
country during the last five years, State-wise; and 
(d) the steps taken by Government to prevent sexual abuse of children and 
protect their rights? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRIMATI KANTI SINGH): (a) and (b) A total of 2113, 
2532 and 2949 cases of child rape were reported in the country during 2001 to 
2003 respectively indicating a rising trend in child rape cases. In Goa, 10, 7 and 
22 cases of child rape were reported during 2001-2003 respectively. Thus, 
overall an increasing trend in child rape cases was observed in Goa also. 
(c) The State and UT wise incidence of child rape reported during 2001 to 2003 
are given in statement (See below). Information for 2004 and 2005 are not 
available with the Government. 
(d) The Government has drawn up plan of Action to combat trafficking and 
commercial sexual exploitation of women and children. The Plan of Action 
consist of action points such as Prevention, Trafficking, Awareness Generation, 
Health Care Services, Education and Child Care, Shelter etc. The State 
Governments have been directed to implement the plan strictly. The Immoral 
Traffic Prevention Act, 1986 is being amended to make it more stringent for 
child sexual abuser. There are constitutional provisions and legislations for 
protection of child rights. The National Policy for Children envisages overall 
development of children. The Government is in process of constituting a 
statutory body known as National Commission for Protection of Child Rights, 
which will ensure effective implementation by the Government for the children in 
various sectors such as health, nutrition, education, water sanitation, protection 
from exploitation and abuse.

Conference on piracy in entertainment industry 
3336. DR. M.A.M. RAMASWAMY: Will the Minister of INFORMATION 
AND BROADCASTING be pleased to state: 
(a) whether in a recent conference of  entertainment industry which was 
attended by him, the industry voiced its serious concern about the piracy 
which is harming the industry badly; 
(b) if so, the other issues voiced by the industry; and 
(c) the steps proposed to be taken to stop piracy and help the enter 
tainment industry come out of the crisis? 
THE MINISTER OF INFORMATION AND BROADCASTING (SHRI S. 
JAIPAL REDDY): (a) and (b) Accord ing to information received from 
Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI), in the recent 
conference of the entertainment industry FRAMES (4-6 April, 2005), the industry 
voiced serious concern regarding piracy, and discussed issues like promotion of 
Indian Entertainment and Media sector globally, exploring co production 
opportunities etc. 
(c) The Copyright Act, 1957, contains inter alia, the legal provisions 
regarding copyright in cinematograph films and music. The responsibility for 
dealing with offences under the Copyright Act rests with the police authorities 
of the State Governments and Union Territory Administrations. Copyright 
Enforcement Cells have been set up in most States/UT Administrations 
headed by a senior police officer to deal with such offences. 
The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting has taken the following steps 
to fight piracy in the film sector: 
O This Ministry has a Plan Scheme to undertake activities relating to anti 
piracy measures. 
O The Ministry has initiated action to formulate appropriate training 
modules for police officers to train them for anti-piracy. 
O Recognizing that high levels of entertainment tax lead to piracy, the 
Committee for Development of th e Entertainment Sector, a sub 
Committee of the State Inform ation Ministers' Conference 
(SIMCON), recommended that the ra te of entertainment tax be 
lowered to a ceiling of 45%. In the recent SIMCON it was felt that 
the ceiling should be further lowered to 25-30%. 
127 

RAJYA SABHA [25 April, 2005] 
O The Committee also recommended appointment of senior police 
officers in States to work in co -ordination with the entertainment 
industry, as nodal officers. 
O During the Budget of 2003-04, audio CDs were exempted from 
excise duty to do away with th e price advantage available to 
pirated CDs. 
O The Public Service Broadcasting Trust has been entrusted with the 
task of making a film on piracy. 
O The Cable Television Networks Regulation Act has been amended 
in 2000, to prohibit a Cable operator from transmitting or re-
transmitting any programme or channel for which the Copyright 
holder has not granted him a license. 
O This Ministry has requested Chief Secretaries of all States to 
advise District Magistrates and Superintendents of Police to include 
anti-piracy measures in their monthly activity reports. 
O This Ministry is consulting FICCI to draft an optical disc law.

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF LAW AND JUSTICE (SHRI K. 
VENKATAPATHY): (a) The number of persons benefited from the legal aid schemes since 
the inception of the State Legal Aid and Advice Boards/State Legal Services 
Authorities, to 31st December, 2004, State-wise, is given in the Statement (see 
below). 
(b) to (d) Section 12 of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 provides for the criteria 
for giving legal services. Accordingly, certain categories of persons such as a member of 
Scheduled Cast, Scheduled Tribe, a woman or a child, a mentally ill or otherwise disabled 
persons etc., are entitled to legal services under the Act without any income limit. Apart 
from such excluded categories as mentioned in clause (a) to (g) of Section 12, clause (h) of 
that section prescribes income limit in other cases. Accordingly, a person in receipt of 
annual income less than Rupees nine thousand or such other higher amount as may be 
prescribed by the State Government, if the case is before a Court other than Supreme 
Court, and less than Rupees twelve thousand or such other higher amount as may be 
prescribed by the Central Government if the case is before the Supreme Court, is entitled 
to legal services under the Act. In exercise of its power under this clause, the Central 
Government has raised the limit of Rupees twelve thousand to Rupees fifty thousand. 
As regards other cases with which State Governments are concerned, different States have 
prescribed different limits. 
Recently, a decision has been taken at the fourth Annual Meet of the State Legal 
Services Authorities held under the aegis of the NALSA on 29.2.2004 & 1.3.2004 at 
Kolkata to raise the income ceiling in terms of Section 12 (h) of the Legal Services 
Act, 1987 (as amended), from Rs. 25,000/- to Rs. 50,000/- per annum in respect of 
cases before the High Court and Courts subordinate thereto.

SHRIMATI AMBIKA SONI:   
SHRI HARISH RAWAT:

SHRI N.K. PREMACHANDRAN:

THE MINISTER OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT (SHRI GHULAM NABI

(b) The Sonia Vihar Water Treatment Plant caters to East Delhi and South

173

(c) and (d) At present Dwarka sub-city is supplied through Nangloi Water 
Treatment Plant. Water supply to this area is expected to improve with the

displacement of water from South Delhi. The commissioning of the Sonia Vihar

Wastage of drinking water 
   3380.   SHRI RAJ MOHINDER SINGH MAJITHA: 
SHRI RAM JETHMALANI: 
Will the Minister of URBAN DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that a wastage of about 40 percent of drinking water 
has been estimated in Delhi; . 
(b) if not, the facts in this regard; 
(c) whether Government have prepared any plan to prevent this wastage of 
drinking water; 
(d) if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) the time schedule fixed for the purpose? 
THE MINISTER OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT (SHRI GHULAM NABI 
AZAD): (a) and (b) The Delhi Jal Boar d (DJB) has informed that sample 
surveys have indicated a high percentage of non-revenue water which includes 
components like physical losses due to leakages, operation losses at water 
treatment plants and distribution system. Unathorised usage and gratuitous 
supplies through Public Water Hydrants/Tankers to J.J. Clusters, unauthorised 
and other colonies. 
(c) and (d) The DJB is taking the fo llowing measures to check loss of 
drinking water:— 
(i) Regular checking of water transmission mains and recording the 
leakages at the Control Room/Water Emergencies set-up in each Zone, 
and attending to them promptly. 
174 

[25 April, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
(ii) Detection of hidden leakages with the help of leak detection 
equipment. 
(iii) Public awareness through media campaign to avoid wastage and adopt 
conservation of water. 
(iv) For checking the wastage/leakage of water, a project named 24x7 has 
been taken up in two zones (South-ll & South-Ill) which covers 12% of 
the total consumers. There is a roll out programme for this project to 
other distribution zones also. 
(v) Installation of bulk meters in the Bulk Water Transmission System. 
(vi) Replacement of old corroded water mains in water Distribution System 
in a phased manner. 
(e) The leakage detection and repair of water distribution lines is a 
continous process. 
Heritage Character of the Lutyen's Delhi 
3381. SHRI B.J. PANDA:Will the Minister of URBAN DEVELOPMENT 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that new master-plan involves new housing activity 
in a big way in the capital; 
(b) whether this would not disturb the heritage character of the Lutyen's zone; 
and 
(c) if so, Government's action plan to protect this heritage character of 
 the capital? 
THE MINISTER OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT (SHRI GHULAM NABI 
AZAD): (a) Delhi Development Authority (DDA) has reported that based on 
projected population of 230 lakhs for Delhi in the year 2021, the draft Master 
Plan for Delhi (MPD) 2021 has estimated the requirement of additional 
housing stock of around 24 lakhs dwelling units. It has been assessed that the 
20 per cent housing need can be met through development of accommodation 
in the adjacent National Capital Region cities, 40 per cent through 
redevelopment/upgradation of existing areas of Delhi and the remaining by way 
of additional new development. 
175 

RAJYA SABHA [25 April, 2005] 
(b) and (c) The draft MPD-2021 recognises the heritage value of the 
Lutyen's Bungalow Zone (LBZ) and recommends its conservation in the process 
of redevelopment of the area. The development in LBZ is governed by the LBZ 
guidelines of 1988. 
Delhi Rent Control Legislation 
3382. SHRI NANA DESHMUKH:W ill the Minister of URBAN 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) the reasons for which implementation of the Rent Control Act for Delhi 
has been delayed for years; 
(b) the specific steps taken by Government to resolve the issues involved; 
(c) whether Government have an assessment of the residential and 
commercial property lying vacant in Delhi at present; 
(d) if so, the details thereof; 
(e) whether absence of a balanced rent control law is one of the reasons for such 
heavy vacancy; and 
(f) if so, the steps taken in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT (SHRI GHULAM NABI 
AZAD): (a) and (b) The Delhi Rent Act, 1995, which was enacted on 
23.08.1995, has not been brought into force so far. Immediately after the Bill 
was passed there were representations against some of the provisions of the said 
Act by a section of tenants, particularly the trader-tenants. The matter was 
examined in details by the Government and it was decided to bring the Act into 
force after effecting amendments to some of its provisions. The Delhi Rent 
(Amendment) Bill, 1997 was accordingly introduced in the Rajya Sabha in July, 
1997. The Bill was referred to the Parliamentary Standing Comm ittee on

    3394. DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY 
 SHRI GIREESH KUMAR SANGHI: 
Will the Minister of URBA N DEVELOPMENT AND POVERTY 
ALLEVIATION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are considering to help the States on low housing 
schemes; 
(b) whether Government propose to provide additional Central Assistance to the States for 
which her Ministry would be nodal agency; 
(c) if so, whether her Ministry would disburse and monitor the Housing for All 
schemes targeted for the economically weaker sections and the lower income group; 
185 

RAJYA SABHA [25 April, 2005] 
(d) whether her Ministry estimates that around 22.4 million houses would be needed 
to keep up with the PM's "Shanghai Vision" for 35 metros; and 
(e) if so, the other steps Government propose to take in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF URBAN 
EMPLOYMENT AND POVERTY ALLEVIATION (KUMARI SELJA): (a) to (e) A 
Centrally Sponsored Scheme called Valmiki Ambedkar Awas Yojana (VAMBAY) is being 
implemented w.e.f. 2.12.2001 in urban areas of all States/UTs. The Scheme has the 
primary objective to facilitate construction and upgradation of dwelling units for slum 
dwellers living below poverty line including Economically Weaker Sections and to provide 
healthy and enabling urban environment through community toilets. 50% of the project 
cost subject to the unit cost ceiling (Rs. 60,000/- for Mega Cities; Rs. 50,000/- for 
metropolitan cities and Rs. 40,000/- for other cities) is released as Central subsidy and 
the balance amount is arranged by the concerned State Governments either from their own 
budget provisions or by taking loan from HUDCO, contribution from beneficiaries etc. There 
is a provision of State Level Coordination Committee (SLCC) to monitor the 
implementation of VAMBAY. 
Futher, Two Million Housing Programme is under operation since 1998-1999 which 
envisages to facilitate construction of 20 lakh additional units every year mainly for the 
Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) and Low Income Group (LIG). Out of which 7 
lakh is taken up for construction in Urban areas and 13 lakh houses is taken up for 
construction in Rural areas. In Urban areas, loan for construction of houses is given by 
Housing & Urban Development Corporation Ltd. (HUDCO), Housing Finance 
Institutions/banks and Cooperative Sector. 
The Working Group of the Planning Commission on Urban Housing for the 10th Plan 
2002-2007 has estimated 22.44 million dwelling units would be required by the end of 
the 10th Plan by way of addition/ upgradation. In order to facilitate construction of 
adequate housing facilities, particularly for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) and 
Low Income Group (LIG), the Government launched the Two Million Housing Programme in 
1998-1999. VAMBAY is also being implemented since 2001 to privide houses for the 
Below Poverty Line Population as well as Economically Weaker Section.

Employment opportunities for Tribals and Women 
3395. SHRI V. HANUMANTHA RAO: Will the Minister of URBAN 
EMPLOYMENT AND POVERTY ALLEVIATION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether any specific schemes have been formulated by Government to create 
employment opportunities in the Urban areas for the tribals and women; 
(b) whether it is a fact that Government have not focused on the stark un-imployment 
and under-empioyment situation prevailing in the cities; 
(c) whether there is anything specific which could be offered to various cities to 
create employment opportunities; 
(d) the details of such plan proposed by Government; and 
(e)the funds spent on this aspect by Government during the year 2004-05? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF URBAN 
EMPLOYMENT AND POVERTY ALLEVIATION (KUMARI SELJA): (a) to (e) In the 
urban areas, Ministry of Urban Employment & Poverty Alleviation is implementing an 
employment oriented Urban Poverty Alleviation Scheme named Swama Jayanti Shahari Rozgar 
Yojana (SJSRY), on all India basis, with effect from 1.12.1997. The scheme envisages to 
provide gainful employment to the urban unemployed and underemployed poor through, 
firstly, encouraging the setting up of self-employment ventures by those who have 
studied upto 9th standard and, secondly, by providing wage employment by utilising 
their labour for construction of socially and economically useful public assets. 
Special attention is given to women, persons belonging to Scheduled 
Castes/Scheduled Tribes and disabled persons under SJSRY. The percentage of 
women beneficiaries under the Scheme should not be less than 30%. Also, the Scheduled 
Tribes must be benefited at least to the extent of the proportion of their strength in the 
local population. 
During 2004-05, Rs. 123.00 crore was utilized under the Swama Jayanti Shahari Rozgar 
Yojana (SJSRY).

3398. SHRI R. KAMARAJ: Will the Minister of URBAN EMPLOYMENT AND 
POVERTY ALLEVIATION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Government propose to introduce a national mission on basic 
services to provide housing and basic infrastructure for the urban slums; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether it is also a fact that Government propose to implement a national 
urban renewal mission programme; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF URBAN 
EMPLOYMENT AND POVERTY ALLEVIATION (KUMARI SELJA): (a) to (d) 
Government is considering to set up a National Urban Renewal Mission to improve the quality 
of urban life. It also proposes to take a comprehensive view to provide basic services to the 
urban poor towards fulfilment of their basic needs, including security of tenure, housing, water 
supply, sanitation, education, health care and social security cover. The detailed modalities 
for the proposed Mission are being worked out.

World Mayors" Conference 
3399. SHRI R. KAMARAJ: Will the Minister of URBAN EMPLOYMENT AND 
POVERTY ALLEVIATION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the Kochi declaration adopted at the World Mayors' 
Conference held recently resolved to strive for poverty alleviation etc.; 
(b) if so, the steps proposed to be taken by Government in this regard; 
(c) whether it is also a fact that the c onference had also decided to allocate 
resources for implementation of city targets focusing on slums and other vulnerable 
groups; and 
(d) if so, the steps taken by Government in this regard? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF URBAN EMPLOY-MENT AND 
POVERTY ALLEVIATION (KUMARI SELJA): (a) and (b) Yes, Sir. The Kochi 
Declaration resolved to strive to closely look at the Millenium Development Goals with regard 
to poverty alleviation etc. Government of India in its Tenth Five Year Plan has fixed the 
monitorable targets of reduc-tion of poverty ratio by 5 percentage points by 2007 and by 15 
percentage points by 2012. Through Swarna Jayanti Shahari Rozgar Yojana (SJSRY), an 
employment oriented urban poverty alleviation programme being implemented by Ministry 
of Urban Employment & Poverty Alleviation, the Government strives to provide 
enterprises as well as skill upgradation training to the urban poor. Under SJSRY, in the Tenth 
Plan, targets for setting up of 4,00,000 micro-enterprises and skill upgradation of 5,00,000 
urban poor in a period of five years has been fixed. 
(c) and (d) Yes, Sir. The Kochi Declaration also resolved to commit and allocate resources 
for the implementation of city targets focusing on slums and other vulnerable groups. The 
Government is committed towards a comprehensive urban renewal and to a massive 
expansion of social housing in towns and cities particularly paying attention to the needs 
of slum dwellers. Under Valmiki Ambedkar Awas Yojana (VAMBAY), housing and 
sanitation needs of the slum dwellers are already being addressed in a targeted manner by 
covering at least one lakh slum families annually who are provided security of tenure and 
basic sanitation facilities.

New Poverty Alleviation Schemes 
3400. SHRI RAVULA CHANDRA SEKAR REDDY: Will the Minister of URBAN 
EMPLOYMENT AND POVERTY ALLEVIATION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have launched any new schemes for poverty alleviation in 
unban areas; 
(b) if so, the salient features thereof including the amount allocated and utilised, 
scheme-wise; 
(c) whether any achievements were made under the schemes; 
(d) if so, the details thereof, State-wise; and 
(e) if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF URBAN 
EMPLOYMENT & POVERTY ALLEVIATION (KUMARI SELJA): (a) and (b) In the 
urban areas, Ministry of Urban Employment & Poverty Alleviation is already implementing 
an employment oriented Poverty Alleviation Scheme named Swarna Jayanti Shahari 
Rozgar Yojana (SJSRY), on all India basis, with effect from 1.12.1997. The scheme 
envisages to provide gainful employment to the urban unemployed and underemployed 
poor through, firstly, encouraging the setting up of self-employment ventures by those who 
have studied upto 9th standard and, secondly, by providing wage employment by 
utilizing their labour for construction of socially and economically useful public assets. 
During 2004-05, Rs. 123.00 crore was allocated and utilized under the Swarna Jayanti 
Shahari Rozgar Yojana (SJSRY). 
(c) to (e) Since inception of the Swarna Jayanti Shahari Rozgar Yojana (SJSRY) in 
1.12.1997 so far 690721 urban poor have been assisted to set up micro enterprises and 701096 
persons have been provided skill training. In addition to this, 532.50 lakhs mandays of work 
have been generated under the wage employment component of SJSRY. State-wise details 
are given in the Statement.

Need to improve punctuality in Indian Airlines flights 
SHRI B.K. HARIPRASAD (Karnataka): Sir, sheer sense of loyalty to nation's 
enterprise prompts me every time to patronise the Indian Airlines for all my journeys, 
but the national carrier seems to take this loyalty for granted. Despite a larger 
fleet, manpower and dedicated ground facilities, the Indian Airlines is losing out to 
private carriers. 
212 

[25 April, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
The punctuality of the Indian Airli nes flights has taken a beating in 
recent times with most of the flights subjected to delays from two to three 
hours. Consider for an in-flight durati on of two hours, you spend two more 
hours at the airport in waiting, apar t from checking in an hour before. 
Technical snags seem to have given wa y to what they now call 'commercial 
delays'. Foggy days of the winter mo nths are no more here, yet they have 
invented this handy stock-phrase for such delays. A delay in the departure of 
the first lap of the journey is causing cascading delays on subsequent flights. 
Because of delays in departure, passengers get stuck-up midway, missing 
connecting flights, which by the theory of probability leave on time. 
Since air passengers pay heavily for the time they save on travel by 
air, it should be incumbent on the ca rrier to compensate for the delays 
monetarily. The existing provisions fo r getting tickets cancelled and refunds 
obtained in case of abnormal delays, re flect the contempt of the carrier in 
adopting a take-it-or-leave-it policy. This  attitude has eroded the credibility of 
the Indian Airlines to a large extent. 
Sir, I urge the Indian Airlines to introduce a better fleet management 
system with accountability for delays squarely fixed and monetary 
compensation for the delays to passengers who do not opt for cancellation or 
refund.

Demand for implementation of SC and ST reservations in Universities 
SHRI PENUMALLI MADHU (Andhra Pradesh): Sir, though there are 
clear orders issued by the Ministry of Human Resource Development and 
UGC to provide for reservation and relaxations in teaching and non-teaching 
posts and admissions in all 17 Central universities, they have hardly been 
implemented. Practically, none of  them have fully implemented the 
constitutionally mandated reservation of 22.5% for the SCs and STs. The 
situation is highly deplorable. 
It is very bad in teaching category. Most of sanctioned posts at 
lecturer-level are not filled under the pretext of non-availability of suitable 
candidates in all Central universities. In almost all universities, only half of the 
sanctioned posts of the lecturers ar e filled, while that of Readers and 
Professors which are invariably double the sanctioned posts, are not filled. 
213 

RAJYA SABHA [25 April, 2005] 
The situation in non-teaching cate gory is not heartening. Majority 
posts in higher category hardly have representation from SCs/STs. Usual 
excuse for this poor representation is lack of suitable/qualified candidates. 
Reservation for lower categories is, to an extent, implemented. But whatever 
recruitment is made, this lower level is used to claim implementation of 
reservation at the aggregate level of the total strength of the university. 
Minority status of a university need not come in the way of 
implementation of reservation for the SC s/STs. After all, rights of minorities 
and those of weaker sections have to be seen as complimenting rather than 
conflicting. The HRD Ministry should make regular monitoring of reservation 
orders, and in case of non-complianc e, strong action must be taken against 
defaulting university and a separate Act on reservations for SCs/STs be 
enacted.

Demand to reduce pressure on metropolitan cities caused by heavy 
influx of migrants 
SHRI SANJAY RAUT (Maharashtra):  I congratulate the Finance 
Minister, Shri P. Chidambaram, for announcing National Urban Renewal 
Mission with an outlay of Rs. 5,500 cror e for seven metropolitan cities in the 
country. However, let me point out that  the efforts of the Mission would not 
yield the desired results unless the Cent re thinks seriously about the problem 
of heavy influx of migrants to major cities. 
Our Constitution has given rights to the citizens to migrate or settle 
anywhere for livelihood. But that does  not mean the taxpayers in the major 
cities should suffer as lakhs of migrants erect shanties in cities like Mumbai 
which are putting tremendous strain on its infrastructure. 
Recently, the Maharashtra Government had to undertake a massive 
demolition drive under which 90,000 sh anties were demolished in Mumbai, 
rendering about two million people homeless. 
214 

[25 April, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
Other metros like Delhi and Kolkat a are facing similar problems. In 
fact, poor people from backward States have to migrate to the cities in search 
of employment just because earning livelihood is difficult in their States. 
It is high time the Central Government took some serious steps to 
address the problems arising out of the mi gration to the cities. The States are 
unable to counter this problem. I would like to request the Union Ministry for 
Urban Development to try and find out some early solution to the problem and 
arrange to create additional funds to the metros for tackling the problems of 
migrants. 
Demand to declare Thirukkural as National Literature 
SHRI P.G. NARAYANAN (Tamil Nadu): Sir, I wish to draw the 
attention of the House to the need for declaring Tamil epic Thirukkural as a 
national literary work to enable the work to be translated in as many regional 
languages as possible. Next to the Bible and Quran, Thirukkural has the 
distinction of being translated in almost  all the world languages. The Bible and 
Quran are religious scripts, but Kura l transcends religio n, caste, creed and 
dwells into issues relating from politics to good governance, importance of 
education and public morality. 
Thiruvalluvar predicted over two thousand years ago that a society 
can prosper only if every individual practises morality. Even in his prayer song, 
the sage does not restrict it to any particular religion, and describes God as a 
principal person of the world. I am sure the translation of this work would help 
to spread humanism. 
The Tamil Nadu Assembly has recently adopted a resolution urging 
the Centre to declare Thirukkural as nat ional literature. I feel honoured that I 
am in a position to raise this issue in this august House and pay my humble 
tribute to the world's oldest literary figure Thiruvalluvar. 
I demand that Thirukkural literature be translated in various 
languages. This attitude alone will go to  prove that we are a pluralistic society 
and all languages are afforded equal opport unities in the Indian State.  So, I 
urge the Centre to declare Thirukkural as national literature.
